messages:
maria_marketing: Hey runtime team — prepping slides and a short benchmark narrative for the webinar next Thursday.
I need validated numbers for MPT-30B quantized (4-bit) — end-to-end p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens for two seq lengths: 512 and 2048. Also need the sample payloads, the exact config used, and the artifacts (raw logs + perf CSVs). Can you run a focused rerun and a couple of sanity checks by Tue EOD so marketing can lock numbers? :pray:

alex_runtime: Clarifying Qs: which exact model artifact (commit/tag) and quantization recipe? We have multiple 4-bit variants (q4_0, q4_1). Also do you want cold-start and cache-warm measurements?

maria_marketing: Good point — use tag mpt-30b@2026-02-11 and the q4_1 recipe (same as prod-quant-2026). Please provide both cold-path (no KV cache warm) and warm-path (after 50 requests prefix warmup). For cost, use our standard cost calc (gpu_time * unit_cost + infra overhead). I pasted the config we want below.

maria_marketing: ```
model: mpt-30b@2026-02-11
quant: q4_1
batching: max_tokens=2048, max_batch=16
seq_lengths: [512, 2048]
warmup_requests: 50
measures: p50,p95,p99,throughput,cost_per_1k_tokens
output_artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/webinar/2026-03-mpt30b-q4_1/
```

alex_runtime: Perfect, thanks. I'll schedule a small matrix: 2 seq lengths x cold/warm x 3 runs each. We should include seed and prompt set — do you have a curated prompt list for webinar examples?

taylor_pm: I have a 40-example prompt set tuned for the marketing narrative (short chat turns, code-gen, summarization). Will upload to s3 and share the path by EOD today. Also request that any big outliers (>2x p95 from baseline) get flagged in the run report.

sam_qa: For sanity checks I'll run a smoke test that validates correctness (sample outputs vs golden subset) plus token-counting sanity and basic perf regression detection. If a run fails smoke, we won't include numbers. Want me to add automatic diffs for top-5 tokens?

maria_marketing: Yes please — include the golden subset diffs and attach a screenshot of a couple representative responses for the slide.

bench-bot: Job created: bench-webinar-1769991234 (matrix: seq512/2048 x cold/warm x 3 runs). ETA ~3h on small dedicated pool. Artifacts will land at s3://redwood-bench/webinar/2026-03-mpt30b-q4_1/<run-id>/

alex_runtime: Queued on dedicated-small (A100s), using runtime v1.9.2. Config snippet for the run: 
```
runtime_version: 1.9.2
hardware: dedicated-small-a100
concurrency: 8
batching_policy: auto
metrics: prometheus, csv, raw_logs
artifact_retention_days: 14
```

alex_runtime: I'll post the first-run summary as comments in this thread when the job finishes. If anything flakey shows up we'll rerun with a tighter isolation window.

maria_marketing: Awesome — if you can also attach a small CSV with the aggregated numbers (p50/p95/p99, cost_1k) and a short one-line explanation of any caveats, that will be enough for the slide. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: Run completed: bench-webinar-1769991234-run-1 
status: SUCCESS
artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/webinar/2026-03-mpt30b-q4_1/bench-webinar-1769991234-run-1/
summary: seq=512 cold p95=112ms cost_1k=$0.32; seq=2048 cold p95=420ms cost_1k=$1.1

alex_runtime: Uploaded aggregate CSV + raw logs to the artifact path. Quick note: seq=2048 warm path improved p95 by ~18% after prefix warmup. Putting the CSV link here: s3://redwood-bench/webinar/2026-03-mpt30b-q4_1/aggregates.csv

maria_marketing: This is great — syncing with the design team now. If we see any regressions in later runs please call them out. Will plan to lock numbers Wed morning for the rehearsal. Thanks everyone!

sam_qa: Going to run the golden-subset diffs now and attach screenshots here when ready.

alex_runtime: FYI, one caveat in the run notes: background autoscaler triggered a small scale-up for a ~30s window during one warm-run. Marked in logs and excluded from aggregate.

maria_marketing: Noted — please include that note in the caveats cell of the CSV.

bench-bot: Artifacts and metadata recorded. Thread archived after run completion. :white_check_mark:
